paragraph: In March 2026 the Instituto de Modernização Administrativa [issued terms of reference for a five-month consultancy to draft a national policy](<https://c2a.portais.gov.ao/uploads/TDR_Contratacao_de_Servico_de_Consultoria_Apoio_Estrategico_e_Juridico_a810d7f256.pdf>) on managing and hosting public data. The policy is to set hosting rules by category of data, and rules on where data must reside. In the last twelve months this is the only step toward a policy that has been found. No source found says a government hosting or cloud policy is adopted and in force. Establishing would need a hosting or cloud policy adopted and in force.

The [two government-cloud data centres the Prime Minister inaugurated on 23 January 2026 are to host all public data](<https://primature.gov.bf/souverainete-numerique-le-premier-ministre-inaugure-deux-datacenters-2/>). A [Prime Minister's circular tells public bodies to give priority to national hosting](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article144800>). In the last twelve months the state ICT agency's board [set the repatriation of administrations' data to them as its course for 2026](<https://anptic.gov.bf/actualites/lanptic-tient-sa-1ere-session-ordinaire-du-conseil-dadministration-de-lannee-2026/>). By July 2026 the ministry had [inventoried 120 public platforms for hosting in the country](<https://www.queenmafa.net/2026/07/26/chantier-zero-donnee-a-lexterieur-120-plateformes-deja-repertoriees/>). Nothing found from the last three years names or counts public bodies moved onto the named hosting. Mature would need a dated source naming or counting bodies moved onto it.

In February 2025 the Deputy Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Communications and Innovation said [the government was developing digital and cloud computing policies](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/84714>). He gave no date for their adoption and did not say who was drafting them. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The same statement [names no government cloud or data centre that public bodies must use](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/84714>). No source found says a government hosting or cloud policy is adopted and in force. Establishing would need a hosting or cloud policy adopted and in force.

On 19 May 2026 the Public Sector Digital Governance Programme (PGNSP) [held a workshop on preparing a National Data Hosting Strategy](<https://fr.linkedin.com/posts/martial-freddy-amakpio-bemade-80b83444_gouvernancenum%C3%A9rique-cloudcomputing-souverainet%C3%A9num%C3%A9rique-activity-7462633363468722176-u68g>), as a participant reported it. In the last twelve months this workshop is the only step toward a policy that has been found. A World Bank-financed project had set a government-wide cloud strategy as a target for December 2026, and [its September 2023 progress report recorded that no strategy had been developed](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099121223050026849/txt/P17462005b395404b0998a03dc83a08ea5d.txt>). No adopted text has been found. Establishing would need a hosting or cloud policy adopted and in force.

The ANSUT document [Politique d'hébergement des données dans le cloud, version 1.0 dated 14 June 2021, was approved on 17 June 2021](<https://www.telecom.gouv.ci/new/uploads/publications/174558607847.pdf>). It sets the procedure for ministries and institutions to host applications in the cloud, and no end or replacement is stated. It names a Microsoft Azure public cloud and the Datacenter eGOUV, both run by ANSUT. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says public bodies must use either, or names a list of approved providers. Operating would need the government to name where public bodies must host.

The Digital Transformation Project terms of reference of [March 2026 say the government is developing a national data hosting strategy](<https://www.mediacongo.net/dpics/filesmanager/jobaof/2026/04-avril/03/ug_260413_02_05.pdf>). UNECA and GIZ are helping. The consultants are to propose hosting and cloud decrees and directives. [CIO Mag reported on 8 November 2023 that the Council of Ministers had adopted a draft decree on the management of national datacenters](<https://cio-mag.com/rdc-inauguration-du-premier-datacenter-national/>). It does not say the decree was later issued. In the last twelve months the terms of reference are the only step toward a policy that has been found. Establishing would need a hosting or cloud policy adopted and in force.

The Supreme Council of Digital Society [adopted the Cloud First Policy on 13 March 2024](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/change/12346-data-localisation-requirement-in-cloud-first-policy-2024>). The policy [entered into force on 22 August 2024](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/change/12346-data-localisation-requirement-in-cloud-first-policy-2024>). It requires data classified top secret or secret to be hosted only within Egypt. In the last twelve months the ICT ministry told a cabinet meeting on 20 September 2026 that it is [preparing a national data-centre strategy with other ministries and bodies](<https://www.youm7.com/story/2026/9/20/رئيس-الوزراء-يتابع-مستجدات-العمل-لعدد-من-مشروعات-تكنولوجيا-المعلومات/7552399>). No source found names a government cloud or data centre that public bodies must use. Operating would need the government to name where public bodies must host.

No stage is set. No government hosting or cloud policy or draft has been found for Eritrea, and no source dated in the last three years says the government has neither. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying the government has no hosting or cloud policy and none is being written.

[In November 2026 the innovation minister restated existing federal directives for public institutions to move off their own server rooms](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/8212/x>). They are to use shared national infrastructure instead. In the last twelve months, in May 2026, [the security agency INSA held a forum on a proposed National Cloud Security Governance Framework](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/information-network-security-administration_insa-cloudsecurity-cybersecurity-activity-7466419690207277056-34la>). [The National Cloud Data Center at the ICT Park in Addis Ababa is to host government services](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/8212/x>) and was still under construction in November 2026. Operating would need the government to name where public bodies must host.

On 26 June 2024 Smart Africa and the National Information Technology Agency [held a validation workshop in Accra to gather stakeholders' input for an enhanced regulatory framework for cloud and data centres](<https://moc.gov.gh/2024/06/26/government-working-to-host-all-data-centres-locally/>), the Ministry of Communications reported. After the workshop the minister said the government is working to have all its data held in other countries hosted in Ghana. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a government hosting or cloud policy is adopted and in force. Establishing would need a hosting or cloud policy adopted and in force.

The Gambia has a [Government Cloud Policy, with a strategy and an implementation plan, dated 2023](<https://publicadministration.desa.un.org/sites/default/files/list-of-files/2025/1.2.1%29%20data%20governance%20-mocde.pdf>), which the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy lists among its policies. The ministry says the [Government Cloud Strategy for 2023 to 2027 builds on the cloud policy](<https://publicadministration.desa.un.org/sites/default/files/list-of-files/2025/1.2.1%29%20data%20governance%20-mocde.pdf>) and aims to modernise government service delivery through cloud adoption. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a government cloud or data centre the policy tells public bodies to use, or a list of approved providers. Operating would need the government to name where public bodies must host.

The [Kenya Cloud Policy, 2025 was signed on 7 April 2025 and took effect on 2 May 2025](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/event/29668-kenya-cloud-policy-2025-entered-into-force-including-authorisation-of-cloud-computing-services>). It [requires sensitive, secret and restricted government data to be stored in Kenya](<https://africaintheroom.substack.com/p/kenyan-citizens-took-a-25-billion>), and State organs have 24 months to migrate systems that are not exempted. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, [applications to be an accredited government cloud provider were open](<https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/bd/corporate/technology/search-for-firm-to-host-sensitive-state-data-on-cloud-begins-5549208>). [The Cabinet Secretary said in August 2026 that institutions must buy only from accredited providers](<https://gaa.go.ke/ministry-urges-public-sector-adopt-ai-cloud-computing>). No list of approved providers has been published. Operating would need the government to name where public bodies must host.

The General Information Authority [held a consultative meeting to review the proposed National Cloud Computing Policy](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2026/01/01/the-general-information-authority-presents-the-proposed-national-cloud-computing-policy-in-collaboration-with-escwa/>), reported in January 2026. [ESCWA reports a further consultative workshop on the draft on 30 December 2025](<https://www.unescwa.org/news/advancing-national-cloud-computing-policy-libya>). In the last twelve months these two consultations are the only dated steps toward the policy that have been found. The meeting agreed to incorporate the feedback into its final version. No source found says a government hosting or cloud policy is adopted and in force. Establishing would need a hosting or cloud policy adopted and in force.

Morocco [has a Cloud First Policy under Digital Morocco 2030](<https://northafricapost.com/92626-moroccos-cloud-first-policy-transforms-digital-governance-and-economic-strategy.html>), the ministry's director of cloud infrastructure said in 2025. [The policy makes cloud the mandatory default for all public-administration technology investments](<https://northafricapost.com/92626-moroccos-cloud-first-policy-transforms-digital-governance-and-economic-strategy.html>). In the last twelve months, [the minister told parliament in December 2025 that it would become the default progressively](<https://www.lavieeco.com/au-royaume/seghrouchni-la-feuille-de-route-cloud-2025-2030-renforce-la-souverainete-numerique-du-royaume/>). No source found names a government cloud or data centre the policy tells public bodies to use, or a list of approved providers. Operating would need the government to name where public bodies must host.

In December 2025 the Minister of Communications and Digital Transformation said the government is [drafting an updated regulatory framework for cloud adoption, to replace current legal restrictions](<https://techafricanews.com/2025/12/04/mozambique-to-build-local-data-centres-and-new-regulations-for-cloud-adoption/>). A [Cloud Computing Regulation approved by Decree No. 72/2025 of 31 December 2025](<https://www.dlapiperafrica.com/en/mozambique/insights/2026/Approval-of-the-Data-Centre-Regulation>) licenses cloud providers. In the last twelve months these are the dated steps found. The [law firm's account of the December 2025 decree](<https://www.dlapiperafrica.com/en/mozambique/insights/2026/Approval-of-the-Data-Centre-Regulation>) describes the licensing of providers and no rule on where public bodies host. Establishing would need a hosting or cloud policy adopted and in force.

On 30 July 2025 Mauritania's data-protection authority [issued deliberation 005/2025 on the minimum conditions for using cloud services abroad](<https://www.apd.mr/%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%85%d8%af%d8%a7%d9%88%d9%84%d8%a9-%d8%b1%d9%82%d9%85-005-2025-%d8%aa%d8%aa%d8%b9%d9%84%d9%91%d9%82-%d8%a8%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%b4%d8%b1%d9%88%d8%b7-%d8%a7/>). Public and private data controllers must obtain its authorisation before processing personal data on foreign cloud services. In the last twelve months, the authority's meeting of 29 April 2026 [had amendments to some of the deliberation's articles on its agenda](<https://www.apd.mr/fr/reunion-mensuelle-ordinaire-de-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-16/>). The [amended text of the deliberation](<https://www.apd.mr/%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%85%d8%af%d8%a7%d9%88%d9%84%d8%a9-%d8%b1%d9%82%d9%85-005-2025-%d8%aa%d8%aa%d8%b9%d9%84%d9%91%d9%82-%d8%a8%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%b4%d8%b1%d9%88%d8%b7-%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%af%d9%86%d9%8a%d8%a7-%d8%a7/>) was published on 30 April 2026. No source found names a government cloud or data centre public bodies must use. Operating would need the government to name where public bodies must host.

[The Procurement Policy Office's Directive No. 53 took effect on 15 December 2020](<https://ppo.govmu.org/Documents/Directives/Directives%202020/Directive%2053.pdf>). [The directive names the Government Online Centre as the hosting for common-use ICT solutions](<https://ppo.govmu.org/Documents/Directives/Directives%202020/Directive%2053.pdf>). [Other data centres or clouds may be used only with the ministry's approval](<https://ppo.govmu.org/Documents/Directives/Directives%202020/Directive%2053.pdf>). It has no end date, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No recent source names the bodies that moved onto the Government Online Centre, or counts them. Mature would need a dated source naming or counting bodies moved onto it.

No stage is set. No government hosting or cloud policy or draft has been found for Malawi. No source since October 2023 says the government has no hosting or cloud policy and none is being written. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying the government has no hosting or cloud policy and none is being written.

On 17 August 2026 the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy [released the National Digital Cloud Policy](<https://techcabal.com/2026/08/18/nigerias-new-cloud-policy-puts-government-at-the-centre-of-its-cloud-market/>). In the last twelve months it [supersedes the Nigeria Cloud Computing Policy 2019, the policy that first introduced Cloud First](<https://techcabal.com/2026/08/18/nigerias-new-cloud-policy-puts-government-at-the-centre-of-its-cloud-market/>). Galaxy Backbone is state-owned. It [will aggregate government cloud demand from registered providers and negotiate framework agreements, with buying through a National Digital Marketplace on which NITDA registers providers](<https://techcabal.com/2026/08/18/nigerias-new-cloud-policy-puts-government-at-the-centre-of-its-cloud-market/>). [In November 2026 the postal service NIPOST said its postcode database is hosted and managed by Galaxy Backbone under the policy](<https://techcabal.com/2026/11/10/nigeria-hybrid-cloud-storage-postcode/>). No source found counts the ministries or agencies that have moved onto Galaxy Backbone.

Rwanda's [Ministerial Instructions N° 001/2012, issued by the Minister in the Office of the President in Charge of ICT](<https://rwandalii.org/akn/rw/act/min/2012/1/eng@2012-03-12>), have been in force since 12 March 2012. [Article 17 of the instructions requires all government IT systems and applications that process, store or provide critical government data to be hosted in the National Data Center](<https://rwandalii.org/akn/rw/act/min/2012/1/eng@2012-03-12>). Article 18 requires institutions with data centres of their own to arrange disaster recovery from it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found from the last three years names or counts public bodies moved onto the named hosting. Mature would need a dated source naming or counting bodies moved onto it.

Commissioning the Diamniadio National Datacenter in June 2021, President Macky Sall [instructed the government to migrate all state data and platforms to it](<https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/senegal-to-migrate-all-government-data-and-applications-to-new-government-data-center/>). He also told it to [repatriate national data hosted outside the country](<https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/senegal-to-migrate-all-government-data-and-applications-to-new-government-data-center/>). The centre is [managed by the state IT agency ADIE](<https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/senegal-to-migrate-all-government-data-and-applications-to-new-government-data-center/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found from the last three years names or counts public bodies moved onto the named hosting. Mature would need a dated source naming or counting bodies moved onto it.

A [ministerial order of 13 September 2023 requires public bodies' software, platforms and infrastructure to be hosted in-house or with cloud providers according to four tiers](<https://www.ancs.tn/sites/default/files/2024-04/Arrete2023_cloud_fr.pdf>). Any other arrangement needs the cybersecurity agency's approval. Circulaire n° 16 of 22 July 2024 [sends sensitive internal systems to a private cloud or to national or sectoral government cloud centres](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/circulaire-n-16-du-22-juillet-2024-portant-sur-la-generalisation-de-ladoption-par-les-structures-publiques-des-solutions-de-cloud-computing-pour-lhebergement-des-logiciels-de/>). In the last twelve months the cybersecurity agency [published its list of labelled providers on 17 September 2026, with six N-Cloud entries](<https://www.webmanagercenter.com/2026/09/22/573106/cybersecurite-et-entreprises-ce-qui-va-changer-pour-les-entreprises-publiques-et-leurs-fournisseurs-prives/>). Nothing found from the last three years names or counts public bodies moved onto the named hosting. Mature would need a dated source naming or counting bodies moved onto it.

The e-Government Authority's [Data Center Standards and Guidelines for Public Institutions, version 2.0, was approved by its board chairperson on 18 February 2026](<https://www.ega.go.tz/uploads/standarddocuments/sw-1773257204-FINAL%20Reviewed_Data%20Center%20Standards%20and%20Guidelines%20for%20Public%20Institutions-18.2.2026.pdf>). The [standard rests on section 25 of the Act](<https://www.ega.go.tz/uploads/standarddocuments/sw-1773257204-FINAL%20Reviewed_Data%20Center%20Standards%20and%20Guidelines%20for%20Public%20Institutions-18.2.2026.pdf>), which requires a public institution to host its systems in a government-approved hosting environment. In the last twelve months this standard is the dated step found. No source found names a government cloud or data centre the policy tells public bodies to use, or a list of approved providers. Operating would need the government to name where public bodies must host.

[NITA-U issued the National Guidelines on Cloud Computing for Government, Ministries, Departments and Agencies in October 2018](<https://oldsite.nita.go.ug/sites/default/files/2022-01/The%20Cloud%20Computing%20Guidelines%20for%20GoU.pdf>). The same guidelines [require those bodies to host information assets classed Official, Secret and Top Secret in the Government Cloud, the National Data Center run by NITA-U](<https://oldsite.nita.go.ug/sites/default/files/2022-01/The%20Cloud%20Computing%20Guidelines%20for%20GoU.pdf>). The document gives no end date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found from the last three years names or counts public bodies moved onto the named hosting. Mature would need a dated source naming or counting bodies moved onto it.

[On 31 May 2024 the communications department gazetted the National Policy on Data and Cloud](<https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/202406/50741gen2533.pdf>), covering national and provincial government and organs of state. It says government data shall be stored in unified, cloud-enabled data centres in designated locations. It names the State Information Technology Agency as the body that sources cloud services for government. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No government cloud or data centre that public bodies must use has been found, and no list of approved providers. Operating would need the government to name where public bodies must host.

[Statutory Instrument No. 43 of 2023, the Electronic Government (General) Regulations, was gazetted on 6 October 2023 under the Electronic Government Act 2021](<https://media.zambialii.org/media/legislation/40749/source_file/a0f9a9fca1dadc67/zm-act-si-2023-43-publication-document.pdf>). Regulation 8 requires every public body to store the personal data it processes on infrastructure domiciled in Zambia. The regulations also [require all public bodies to integrate their services with the Government Service Bus](<https://media.zambialii.org/media/legislation/40749/source_file/a0f9a9fca1dadc67/zm-act-si-2023-43-publication-document.pdf>). They do not say which hosting to use. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need the government to name where public bodies must host.

At the first workshop of government ICT directors in May 2026, the ICT minister, Tatenda Mavetera, [set out a Zimbabwe Government Cloud as a companion policy to a cloud-first and mobile-first direction](<https://spikedmedia.co.zw/minister-mavetera-issues-five-landmark-directives-at-inaugural-ict-directors-workshop/>). It is to end ministries buying their own servers and to consolidate the state's infrastructure. In the last twelve months this announcement is the only step toward a policy that has been found. No adopted policy, circular or regulation has been found. Establishing would need a hosting or cloud policy adopted and in force.
